beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Selamat pagi, Liam. One Claude prompt. An animated BCL-2 selectivity diagram — three guardian shapes, one plug, one displaced captive, one trigger.

props.command: claude "Port the bcl-selectivity plate from plates_gen.py p11() into Manim. 3 stacked BLUE guardian shapes with notches. ORANGE plug fits middle notch, displacing VERM captive to GREEN trigger."

beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — what BCL-2 family selectivity IS
beats.narration_text: The BCL-2 family has multiple anti-death guardians, and each holds a different pro-death partner. To trigger apoptosis you have to displace a specific captive from a specific guardian. The plate shows the lock-and-key geometry: only one plug fits one guardian's notch.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — three BLUE guardian shapes stacked vertically; each with a notch; captive wedges inside; lock-and-key label

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — venetoclax selectivity mechanism
beats.narration_text: Venetoclax is selective for BCL-2 specifically — not BCL-XL, not MCL-1. That selectivity is the whole mechanism. It displaces only the captive held by BCL-2, freeing it to trigger the death cascade. Cells that depend on BCL-2 die; cells that depend on other guardians survive.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — venetoclax targets BCL-2 only; top and bottom guardians intact; middle guardian loses captive; 'selectivity is the mechanism' label

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the bcl-selectivity plate from plates underscore gen dot py p eleven into Manim. Three stacked BLUE guardian shapes with notches. Top and bottom hold SKY captive wedges. An ORANGE plug fits the middle notch, displacing a VERM captive that moves to a GREEN trigger. Animate: guardians, then plug approach, then displacement.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_BclSelectivity class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The three guardians are RoundedRectangles. Each notch is simulated with a white Rectangle overlapping the right edge — the simplest approach. SKY wedge polygons sit inside top and bottom guardians. The VERM displaced captive and ORANGE plug are separate objects. The choreography is four plays: guardians in, captives in, plug arrow grows, trigger assembles. One scene, four acts.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_BclSelectivity
props.code:
# BCL-2 selectivity — 3 guardians, 1 plug, 1 displaced captive
BLUE="#0072B2"; SKY="#56B4E9"; VERM="#D55E00"
GREEN="#009E73"; ORANGE="#E69F00"
GY_POS=[[-2,2.2,0],[-2,0,0],[-2,-2.2,0]]

class B05_BclSelectivity(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    # 3 BLUE guardian rectangles
    guardians=[RoundedRectangle(width=2.8,height=1.4,corner_radius=0.2,
               color=BLUE,fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.16,
               stroke_width=3.2).move_to(p) for p in GY_POS]
    # notch cutout (white overlay on right edge)
    notches=[Rectangle(width=0.6,height=0.52,color=WHITE,fill_color=WHITE,
             fill_opacity=1,stroke_width=0).move_to(
             [p[0]+1.4,p[1],0]) for p in GY_POS]
    # SKY captives in top and bottom
    sky_wedges=[_wedge([p[0]+1.0,p[1],0],SKY) for p in [GY_POS[0],GY_POS[2]]]
    # VERM displaced captive next to middle guardian
    verm_cap=_wedge([-0.2,0,0],VERM)
    # ORANGE plug at far right
    plug=_wedge([4.5,0,0],ORANGE,size=0.38)
    trigger=Circle(radius=0.4,color=GREEN,fill_color=GREEN,
                   fill_opacity=0.3,stroke_width=2.8).move_to([3.0,-0.5,0])
    plug_arrow=Arrow([4.5,0,0],[-0.4,0,0],color=ORANGE,buff=0.1)
    disp_arrow=Arrow([-0.2,0,0],[2.6,-0.5,0],color=VERM,buff=0.1)
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(g) for g in guardians],lag_ratio=0.2))
    self.play(*[FadeIn(n) for n in notches],*[FadeIn(w) for w in sky_wedges],FadeIn(verm_cap),FadeIn(plug))
    self.play(GrowArrow(plug_arrow))
    self.play(GrowArrow(disp_arrow),Flash(trigger.get_center(),color=GREEN,line_length=0.3,num_lines=8,flash_radius=0.6),FadeIn(trigger))

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_BclSelectivity — guardians, captives, plug approach, trigger
beats.narration_text: Run it. Three guardians fade in — BLUE, stacked vertically. SKY captives inside top and bottom. The VERM captive sits next to the middle one, already displaced. The ORANGE plug appears at right, arrow grows toward the middle guardian's notch. A second arrow shows the displaced captive moving toward the GREEN trigger. The geometry makes the selectivity argument without a label.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: plug moves from right into the middle notch — animate its position change. Middle captive is pushed out and travels to the trigger — animate that movement too. Top and bottom captives stay still. Emphasize selectivity. Trigger assembles with a slight scale bounce.

props.command:
claude "Revise: plug moves from right into the middle notch (animate position).
Middle captive is pushed out and travels to the trigger (animate movement).
Top and bottom captives stay still — emphasize SELECTIVITY. Trigger assembles
with a slight scale bounce."

beats.act: OUTPUT — revised animation with plug movement
beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_BclSelectivityFit — plug moves, captive travels, trigger bounces
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. All three guardians build with their captives first. Then the ORANGE plug slides from the right into the middle notch — you see it enter. The middle captive gets pushed out and travels toward the trigger. Top and bottom captives stay perfectly still — that is selectivity made visible. The trigger assembles with a scale bounce. Three locks, one key, one consequence.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: Three locks, one key that fits only one. The motion showed what selectivity means physically: the plug engages one notch, one captive moves, and the other two stay perfectly still. Claude ported the plate geometry in one prompt and added the animated displacement in one revision. The pattern: build the locks, move the key, show what doesn't move. Strip that and you can animate any receptor-ligand selectivity argument.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — summary: 3 locks, 1 key; selectivity = what doesn't move; strip pattern for any receptor-ligand

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a fourth guardian shape — MCL-1 — and animate a second plug that cannot fit any of the four notches because its shape is wrong. Show it bouncing off. Why run it? Because the failure mode is as important as the success. Drugs that fail BCL-2 selectivity often do so because they can't engage the BH3-binding groove of a specific family member. The animation would make the shape mismatch argument physical — and would set up the next question, which is why MCL-1 is so much harder to drug.

props.command:
claude "Add a 4th guardian (MCL-1). Animate a second plug that fails to fit any
notch — shape mismatch, it bounces off. Show what a non-selective drug
looks like geometrically. Why does MCL-1 resist most BH3 mimetics?"
